newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL negotiates Sky Network TV purchase.
newsitem.headline: INL negotiates Sky Network TV purchase.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Friday it was in negotiations to buy a "substantial shareholding" in New Zealand pay-TV operator Sky Network Television Ltd.
Chairman Sir Colin Maiden made the announcement to the company's annual meeting in Wellington, where he also said trading profit was ahead of last year.
Sky is New Zealand's dominant pay-TV operator.

INL said it was in negotiations with a consortium of New Zealand companies, Heatley Jarvis Investments Ltd, Tappenden Construction Ltd and Todd Corporation, and the U.S.-based HKP Partnership, to purchase a substantial shareholding in Sky.
Maiden said in a later statement to the New Zealand Stock Exchange there were still a number of issues to be resolved but a statement was being issued in the interest of an informed market.
If the negotiations were successful, Sky would be a major investment for Independent Newspapers in the television field. Another announcement would be made when negotiations were concluded.
Chief Executive Mike Robson said INL had strengthened its balance sheet and was well positioned to make the major commitment that the Sky purchase would require.
"I believe INL is well positioned to go forward," Robson said, adding the company would benefit from a further fall in newsprint prices.
He said magazine distributor Gordon and Gotch continued to lag behind expectations in Australia.
The Houston community newspaper group in the United States was trading ahead of budget and ahead of last year.
